slides.1.title: Setúbal & Palmela DOC Regional Map
slides.1.description: The Península de Setúbal on the south bank of the Tejo estuary: Palmela (Castelão reds) and Setúbal (one of the world's most famous Moscatel origins)
slides.3.title: Moscatel de Setúbal DOC: Liquid Honey
slides.3.html:
Moscatel de Setúbal is one of Portugal's greatest sweet wines, made on the limestone soils of the northern peninsula using a distinctive method.

🔬 Winemaking

  • Uses Muscat varieties (called Moscatel in Portugal): mainly Moscatel de Setúbal (= Muscat of Alexandria) and Moscatel Roxo (a purple variety)
  • Timing of fortification: grape spirit is added partway through fermentation, retaining residual sugar, with a final alcohol of 17-18%
  • Muscat skin maceration: before bottling, extra fresh grape skins are steeped in the wine for 3-6 months, adding intense floral and Muscat aromas; this is a unique step in Moscatel de Setúbal

🌸 Style types

  • Young (5-10 years): deep gold, Muscat floral notes, orange blossom, apricot, fig, silky and sweet
  • Aged (20-40 years): deep amber, toffee, walnut, roasted coffee, orange peel, extremely complex
  • Moscatel Roxo: a purple variety, darker in colour, with distinctive aromas of rose, raspberry and spice

🏰 Leading producers

  • José Maria da Fonseca: the most important producer of Moscatel de Setúbal, dating back to 1834, with aged Moscatels from vintages over a century old
  • Bacalhôa Vinhos de Portugal: a large group; the JP (José Pinto) Azeitão estate also produces fine Moscatel
slides.4.title: Moscatel de Setúbal vs. Other Portuguese Sweet Wines
slides.4.items.0.desc: The most unique: made with fresh grape skin maceration, with the most pronounced Muscat floral character. Can age for 50-100 years. From the limestone Setúbal peninsula
slides.4.items.1.label: Vintage Port (sweet)
slides.4.items.1.desc: Deep purple-black, blackberry, chocolate, tobacco, with high tannin structure. A fortified sweet wine from the Douro's schist terraces, ageing for 20-50 years
slides.4.items.2.desc: Oxidative and fortified, with caramel, honey and tropical fruit, and the distinctive Estufagem heating process. The sweetest Madeira style
slides.4.items.3.desc: Setúbal's own purple Muscatel variety, with rose and raspberry aromas; one of Portugal's rarest sweet wines, made in tiny quantities
slides.5.question: What unique step in Moscatel de Setúbal winemaking is not found in other Portuguese fortified sweet wines?
slides.5.options.1: Heating to 50°C in stainless steel tanks
slides.5.options.2: Steeping extra fresh grape skins for 3-6 months before bottling
slides.5.explanation: The unique step in Moscatel de Setúbal is that, after fortification and before bottling, fresh Moscatel grape skins are added to the wine and left to macerate for 3-6 months. This extra skin contact greatly intensifies the Muscat floral aromas, and is not used in other Portuguese fortified sweet wines such as Port or Madeira.
slides.6.question: Which winery is the most important producer of Moscatel de Setúbal, dating back to 1834 and holding aged Moscatels from vintages over a century old?
slides.6.explanation: José Maria da Fonseca, founded in 1834, is the most important historic producer of Moscatel de Setúbal. It holds several aged Moscatels more than a century old, among the most precious living history in Portuguese wine.
slides.7.title: Setúbal and Palmela: Additional Rules
slides.7.html:
The two DOCs of the Península de Setúbal each have clear variety thresholds:

  • Moscatel de Setúbal: whites must contain ≥ 67% Moscatel de Setúbal (Muscat d’Alexandrie), and reds (Roxo) must contain ≥ 67% Moscatel Roxo; a single-variety label requires 85%
  • After fermentation and fortification, the wine continues to macerate on Muscat skins for about 6 months, giving intense floral aromas; it is then aged in large wooden vats for up to about 5 years before release, and some wines can exceed 20 years
  • Palmela DOC: reds are based on Castelão, legally at least 66.7%; whites use plenty of Fernão Pires and Arinto, and international varieties are also permitted

Based on compiled data from 2011-2012.
